stories.head: GTM teams are losing track of their AI agents
stories.plain: As AI agents multiply across sales, marketing, and ops stacks, most GTM teams have no clear inventory of what those agents do, who owns them, or what decisions they're making. This is a governance gap that can expose companies to compliance risk and wasted spend — and it's growing fast.

stories.head: Iterable Fall Release adds native RCS, Nova Conversations, and new AI Agents
stories.plain: Iterable's major platform update links customer data, conversations, and AI intelligence into a single loop. New features include an Integrations Hub, RCS messaging, Nova Conversations, and Nova Intelligence Agents — meaning the platform can now act on customer signals, not just send messages. This reshapes how the CEP category is bought.

stories.head: AAMP 2.3 forces CMOs to rethink compliance when AI agents choose vendors
stories.plain: SafeGuard Privacy's Richy Glassberg explains how the AAMP 2.3 standard changes privacy compliance when AI agents make vendor decisions at machine speed — no human picks up the phone. CMOs need new governance frameworks because existing contracts and consent workflows were built for human buyers.

stories.head: TransUnion: only 13% of marketers have fully scaled AI due to fragmented data
stories.plain: TransUnion EVP Matt Spiegel identifies a confidence-readiness paradox: marketers are optimistic about AI but only a tiny fraction have scaled it. The culprit is fragmented customer data and siloed teams — a direct warning that CDP readiness, not model quality, is the real bottleneck to AI ROI.

stories.head: Why treating LLMs like thinking partners produces bad marketing outputs
stories.plain: Vague, conversational prompts cause hallucinations and unreliable content when teams treat LLMs as collaborators rather than structured tools. The article offers a practical reframe for how marketing teams should engineer prompts — directly affecting the quality and safety of AI-generated campaigns.

stories.head: GTM teams are losing track of their AI agents
stories.plain: As AI agents multiply across the GTM stack, most teams have no central inventory of what each agent does, who owns it, or what decisions it makes. This visibility gap creates real governance risk — rogue agents can act on stale data or break compliance rules with no one noticing until damage is done.

stories.head: Iterable Fall Release adds native RCS, Nova Conversations, Integrations Hub, and new AI Agents
stories.plain: Iterable's biggest update yet wires customer data, conversations, and intelligence into a continuous learning loop. New Nova Intelligence Agents act on signals in real time; a native Integrations Hub removes the need for middleware. This reshapes how mid-market brands buy and configure a customer engagement platform — fewer point tools, one memory layer.

stories.head: OpenAI testing third-party-style tracking in ChatGPT ads
stories.plain: OpenAI is piloting a persistent identifier for ad measurement inside ChatGPT, mirroring third-party cookie logic in an AI interface. If it ships, it resets how marketers attribute conversions from generative AI surfaces and reopens consent debates that brands thought were settled after the cookie phase-out.

stories.head: Expert Mode: AI media agents can't pick up the phone — what AAMP 2.3 means for CMO compliance
stories.plain: SafeGuard Privacy's Richy Glassberg explains how AAMP 2.3 forces vendor compliance checks to happen at machine speed — but AI media agents can't negotiate consent the way a human buyer can. CMOs now need automated privacy guardrails baked into agentic buying workflows, not bolted on after the fact.

stories.head: Dataiku launches Agent Management to track and govern AI agents across platforms
stories.plain: Dataiku's new Agent Management layer auto-discovers agents built on any platform, measures their business value, and flags risk in one dashboard. It directly answers the enterprise need for cross-vendor agent oversight — making it easier to buy, audit, and retire AI agents without rebuilding governance from scratch for each tool.

month.skicker: 30-day synthesis · the shape underneath the feed

themes.head: AI Agents Are Escaping Oversight
body: Go-to-market teams are deploying AI agents faster than they can track them, creating a growing blind spot where autonomous software makes customer-facing decisions with no clear owner. The problem is not capability — it is accountability infrastructure: most orgs lack registries, audit logs, or governance policies for the agents already running in production.

Dataiku's new Agent Management layer and the broader push for AI governance frameworks signal that the industry is starting to treat agent sprawl as a systemic risk, not just a technical inconvenience. Teams that build oversight tooling now will have a measurable edge when regulators or boards start asking who approved the bot that emailed a million customers.

themes.head: Proprietary Data Is the Real AI Moat
body: With foundation models becoming commoditised, the competitive question has shifted from which LLM you use to what you feed it. TransUnion's data-readiness paradox — high AI confidence, low data quality — captures exactly why most AI projects underdeliver: the model is fine; the inputs are not.

Partnerships like Evalueserve–Databricks and Iterable's persistent customer memory architecture are practical responses to this reality. Brands that invest in clean, unified, proprietary data pipelines now are building advantages that competitors running the same off-the-shelf models simply cannot copy.

themes.head: AI Search Is Rewriting the Purchase Funnel
body: AI-powered search engines and ChatGPT-style interfaces are now actively recommending against products, summarising reviews, and short-circuiting the click-through journey that ecommerce has relied on for two decades. Marketers who optimised for keywords and category pages are finding those pages increasingly bypassed.

OpenAI testing third-party-style ad tracking inside ChatGPT shows that the platforms themselves are scrambling to monetise this new funnel — which means brands need a presence in AI-generated answers, not just in blue-link results. B2B brands pivoting to creator video partly do so because authentic human content surfaces better in AI-curated feeds than polished brand copy.

themes.head: The AI Coworker Model Goes Mainstream
body: Products are shipping under explicit "coworker" framing — Snappy AI for financial advisors, Adobe tools embedded in Gemini and Claude — signalling a shift from AI as a feature inside software to AI as a named team member with a role. This changes hiring logic: the question is no longer just "what tools do we buy" but "what human skills complement the AI colleague."

The MarTech skills survival guide and Klaviyo CMO Jamie Domenici's commentary converge on the same point: strategic judgment, brand stewardship, and cross-functional coordination are the roles humans retain when the assistant writes the first draft of nearly everything. Orgs that reskill now avoid the painful realisation later that they optimised humans out of the decisions that matter most.

themes.head: Platform Ecosystems Replace Point-Solution Stacks
body: Adobe embedding creative tools into Gemini and Claude, ZoomInfo integrating natively with Replit via GTM.AI, and UserTesting piping human insight directly into AI workflows all follow the same architectural logic: capabilities travel to wherever the work happens rather than forcing users into a separate destination app. The integration layer is becoming the product.

Workato's Gartner Customers' Choice recognition for iPaaS and the CSG/Netcracker orchestration honours reflect buyer appetite for platforms that orchestrate across the whole journey rather than optimise a single channel. Marketers evaluating new tools should now ask not "what does this do" but "how deeply does this connect to everything else we already run."

month.takeaway: Across every corner of the stack, the defining pressure of this moment is that AI is moving faster than the governance, data quality, and human skill development needed to make it trustworthy — and the teams that close that gap first will own the next era of growth.
